nodes.label: Deterministic Match Scoring
nodes.rationale: Scoring is deterministic and explainable so an LLM never directly chooses the final numeric score; a deterministic aggregator owns the number and validators stay authoritative over agent output, keeping results reproducible and defensible rather than an opaque ATS prediction.

nodes.label: Truth-Constrained Tailoring
nodes.rationale: Every generated resume statement must reference verified sourceFactIds; the model may rephrase/reorder/emphasize/omit verified content but may never invent employers, dates, skills or metrics, so NEW_CLAIM proposals are rejected by default to preserve candidate truthfulness.

nodes.label: Docling Document Parsing
nodes.rationale: Docling is the only document-intelligence library in the POC; a second parser (OpenDataLoader, Marker, PyMuPDF, pdfplumber) is forbidden until benchmark evidence justifies it, avoiding premature dependency sprawl.

nodes.label: Candidate Fact Verification with A4 Source
nodes.rationale: Profile verification shows the rendered uploaded resume as paginated A4 source pages alongside extracted facts so users can compare extraction with source before facts become verified; unverified facts cannot support generated claims.
nodes.norm_label: candidate fact verification with a4 source

nodes.label: Approved Immutable Fill Plan
nodes.rationale: AI output never manipulates the page directly; the service worker executes only a schema-validated, user-approved immutable fill plan through an ATS adapter, and editing a value creates a new proposed version requiring re-approval.

nodes.label: ATS Adapter Contract
nodes.rationale: Page-specific ATS logic is kept out of the UI behind a capability-based adapter contract; unsupported capabilities degrade to clear manual instructions rather than guessed automation.

nodes.label: GreenhouseAdapter
nodes.rationale: Greenhouse is the first ATS-specific adapter; Ashby and Workday are deferred until volume justifies the maintenance cost.

nodes.label: Zustand UI/Workflow Store
nodes.rationale: Zustand is an in-memory projection per React surface, not a cross-context database; Chrome storage and IndexedDB remain the durable repositories so service-worker suspension or a closed tab never destroys an application record.

nodes.label: AI Provider Interface
nodes.rationale: One internal provider interface with server-side credentials and a model allowlist; provider failure never silently falls back to another provider, and provider/model provenance is recorded on every AI-assisted artifact.

nodes.label: CriticAgent
nodes.rationale: CriticAgent reviews each tailoring proposal for relevance, semantic drift, and unsupported claims before deterministic validation, but critic approval never overrides schema, sourceFactIds, classification, or truth validators.

nodes.label: Application Identity (applicationId/jobFingerprint/tabId)
nodes.rationale: An application has a durable applicationId and jobFingerprint (normalized company+title+location+URL); a Chrome tabId is only a temporary browser binding, so a reopened tab reconnects to the durable record without creating duplicates.

nodes.label: Untrusted Page-Content Trust Boundary
nodes.rationale: Job-page content, labels, hidden DOM text, JSON-LD and application questions are untrusted data never instructions; content is sanitized and delimited before AI use so embedded instructions cannot change system behavior (prompt-injection defense).

nodes.label: A4 Preview and PDF Generation
nodes.rationale: The exact same generated HTML/CSS drives both the sandboxed A4 preview and Playwright PDF generation to avoid preview/PDF drift, using a single ATS-safe template in the POC.

nodes.label: Never Invent Candidate Facts Principle
nodes.rationale: A locked product decision: the system must never invent candidate facts and sensitive demographic answers are never inferred; deterministic truth validators remain authoritative over all agent output across scoring, tailoring, and filling.

nodes.label: User-Controlled Final Submission Principle
nodes.rationale: The extension never automatically clicks the final Submit button; the user preserves control over all generated content and form filling, and final submission always remains a user action on the portal.
